results.result: The study utilized 176 Diversity Outbred (DO) mouse embryonic stem cell samples profiled for genotype (via GigaMUGA array with 68,413 imputed haplotype calls), gene expression (RNA-seq, log2-TPM), and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq, TMM normalized). The DO population segregates millions of variants from eight founder strains with linkage disequilibrium blocks approaching TAD size.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C6, C24-C27, and C78-C84 collectively describe the experimental system, sample size, data types, and processing methods. The methods are clearly documented with appropriate citations and normalization procedures. The characterization of the DO population and its genetic properties is well-established in prior literature.

results.result: Regression modeling of 39,021,625 gene-genotype-ATAC combinations identified 27,509 significant non-additive interaction models (Bonferroni adjusted p < 1×10⁻⁷), representing 0.07% of tested models but four orders of magnitude more than expected under a null distribution, demonstrating that genetic-epigenetic interactions are common throughout the genome.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C29 and C7 provide clear statistical evidence with appropriate multiple testing correction. The comparison to null expectations (C29) and the enrichment of significant results strongly support the conclusion that interactions are widespread. The stringent significance threshold addresses concerns about false positives from massive multiple testing.

results.result: Genetic-epigenetic interactions occur locally, with 49% of significant models having elements within 4 Mb of the affected gene, and models with at least one element within the same TAD as the gene being 3.7 times more likely to reach significance (3.3% vs 0.9%), demonstrating that interaction locality corresponds to TAD structure.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C32, C8-C9 demonstrate clear enrichment of intra-TAD interactions with appropriate statistical comparisons. The 3.7-fold enrichment is substantial and the finding that co-localization of variants and ATAC peaks is not the primary driver (C31, <10%) strengthens the TAD-based interpretation.

results.result: Non-additive interacting models represent 32.29% of significant intra-TAD models, with 41.81% of ATAC-seq peaks exclusive to interacting models, while genetic variants show more overlap between model types (26.35% shared between interacting and additive models).
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C35 quantify the distribution of regulatory elements across model types. The high proportion of ATAC-seq peaks exclusive to interacting models (C35) supports the conclusion that interaction analysis reveals regulatory elements not detectable by single-omics approaches. The data are clearly presented with reference to figures.

results.result: TAD boundaries constrain genetic-epigenetic interactions, with 52,511 ATAC-seq peaks sharing a TAD with their interacting gene versus 24,229 in different TADs (odds ratio 1.48, p < 2.2×10⁻¹⁶). The likelihood of interaction is most strongly defined by 3D TAD structure rather than linear DNA sequence, and TAD-based searches consistently outperform linear sequence-based searches.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C37, C10, C44-C45 provide strong statistical evidence for TAD-based constraints with highly significant enrichment. The comparison between TAD-based and linear search methods (C45) directly tests the hypothesis. The identification of 29 highly interactive ATAC peaks (C38, >200 interactions each) exclusively within TADs provides additional support.

results.result: To capture 95% of inter-TAD interactions, a window of ~2.1 Mb upstream and ~2.6 Mb downstream of gene TSS is required. Interacting ATAC-seq peaks are enriched in gene bodies (65.37%), exons (34.41%, especially first exons), promoters (24.06%), and enhancers (6.09%).
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C43 provide clear quantitative characterization of interaction distances and genomic distributions. The window size determination (C39) is data-driven and the genomic feature enrichments (C40-C43) are well-documented, though the enhancer overlap is relatively low (C43, 6.09%), which may reflect incomplete enhancer annotations or cell-type specificity.

results.result: 24.31% of genes (12,437 genes) have a TAD boundary close upstream to their TSS, which may explain differences between TAD-based and linear search methods near gene promoters.
results.evaluation: Claim C46 provides a clear quantitative finding with figure support. This observation helps explain the unexpected depletion of interactions immediately flanking genes noted in the analysis, though the definition of 'close upstream' could be more precisely specified.

results.result: Interaction effects were of greater absolute value than ATAC-seq effects 61.24% of the time. Models indicating redundancy or interference were most common (40.53-39.54%), synergistic effects occurred in 17.02% of models, and unexpectedly, increased ATAC-seq signal had negative effects on gene expression in 40.76% of models.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C50 characterize the magnitude and directionality of interaction effects with clear percentages. The finding that interaction effects often exceed main effects (C47) is notable and well-quantified. The high proportion of negative ATAC effects (C50) is surprising but documented, motivating further investigation in subsequent analyses.

results.result: ATAC-seq peaks with negative effects on gene expression are enriched for CTCF-binding motifs (53.3% vs 35.3% in positive effectors, p < 2.0×10⁻¹⁴) and SMAD3-binding sites (p < 1.5×10⁻⁸). Negative effector CTCF motifs contain SNPs at much higher rates (96.1% vs 18.0% for positive effectors, p < 2.2×10⁻¹⁶) and show minimal overlap with ENCODE CTCF ChIP-seq data (2.04% and 1.87% vs 17.45% and 16.20%).
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C54 provide strong statistical evidence for motif enrichment with highly significant p-values. The dramatic difference in SNP content between negative and positive effector CTCF motifs (C53, 96.1% vs 18.0%) and low overlap with existing ChIP-seq data (C54) support the hypothesis of strain-specific CTCF binding disruption. The motif analysis methods are appropriately cited.

results.result: The Platr2 TAD contains 1031 significant interaction models (179 for Platr2 expression itself), with motif enrichment analysis identifying Smad3-binding motifs at 16 sites and CTCF-binding motifs at 15 sites, suggesting modulation of CTCF-binding strength. Previous studies identified Platr2 as a trans-eQTL regulator of developmental genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C57 provide a detailed case study with clear quantification and motif analysis. The connection to prior work (C56) provides biological context. However, the interpretation that motifs 'suggest modulation of CTCF-binding strength' (C57) is somewhat speculative without direct binding measurements in this specific context.

results.result: CTCF ChIP-seq in four DO founder strains (C57BL/6J, CAST/EiJ, PWK/Ph, WSB/EiJ) identified 65,541 significant peaks (68.21% of results), with 90.65% overlapping known TAD boundaries. Only 52% of peaks were shared across all four strains (48% strain-specific), and 13% showed high variance in binding intensity (fold enrichment variance >10). PCA showed strain clustering by subspecies.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C64 and C89 describe the ChIP-seq validation experiment with clear methods and results. The finding of substantial strain-specific CTCF binding (48%, C62) is well-documented. However, one PWK and one WSB sample were lost, which may affect power for those strains. The overlap with existing data (C63, 36.45%) and TAD boundaries (C61, 90.65%) provides validation.

results.result: DO genotype at CTCF-binding sites predicts strain-specific CTCF binding intensity, with predictive power increasing from 16% (all peaks) to 31% (peaks in ATAC-seq regions) to 37% (non-additive interacting models) to 39% (negative effector peaks). In high-density interaction regions, the gap between negative and positive effectors widened to 44% vs 27%, confirming strain-specific CTCF binding linked to genetic variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C69, C13, and C74 demonstrate progressive enrichment of predictive power through increasingly refined subsets, providing strong validation of the regression model's ability to identify functionally relevant genetic-epigenetic interactions. The hierarchical analysis is logical and the trend is clear, though the correlation percentages represent proportions of significant t-tests (p<0.05) rather than effect sizes.

results.result: The study demonstrates bidirectional inference: stable 3D genome structure (TADs) effectively guides searches for regulatory elements, and conversely, regulatory elements in genetically diverse populations provide a means to infer 3D genome structure. Patterns of genetic-epigenetic interaction reflect TAD structure, with TAD boundaries being more important than chromatin density, and linear proximity being insufficient for identifying gene-regulatory associations.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C12, C71-C73, C16, and C77 represent the major conceptual conclusions of the study. These are well-supported by the collective evidence from interaction enrichment within TADs (C32, 3.7-fold), superior performance of TAD-based searches (C45), and validation via CTCF ChIP-seq (C65-C69). The bidirectional inference claim is substantiated by both the use of known TADs to find interactions and the ability to predict CTCF binding from interaction models.

results.result: Open chromatin regions participating in the most significant regression models are enriched for developmental genes and the TAD-forming CTCF-binding complex, providing an opportunity for statistical inference of shifting TAD boundaries during early development.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C15 state enrichment for developmental genes and CTCF-binding complex, which is supported by the motif analysis (C51, C15). However, the claim about 'opportunity for statistical inference of shifting TAD boundaries operating during early development' is speculative. The study uses mESCs at a single developmental stage, so direct evidence for shifting boundaries during development is not provided. This would require time-course or differentiation experiments.

results.result: Integrating multi-omics data analysis in genetically diverse populations allows for greater specificity and modeling of complex regulatory interactions.
results.evaluation: Claim C70 is a general methodological conclusion supported by the entire study. The demonstration that 41.81% of ATAC-seq peaks are exclusive to interacting models (C35) and that interaction models better predict CTCF binding (C67-C68) provides evidence for this claim. This represents a valid inference from the presented data.

results.result: Statistical and analytical methods included Bonferroni-adjusted p-value cutoff of p < 1×10⁻⁷ for significant models, TAD data from Dixon et al. 2012 (mm9 lifted to mm10), motif analysis via MEMEsuite (MEME, STREME, Tomtom), and CTCF ChIP-seq following Oomen et al. 2019 protocols.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C88 document key methodological choices with appropriate citations. The Bonferroni correction (C85) is appropriately stringent given the massive multiple testing. The use of published TAD data (C86) and established protocols (C87-C88) is well-documented. However, the TAD data are from a single B6 mESC line, which may not capture strain-specific variation that the study aims to detect.

results.result: The manuscript reviews established knowledge about genetic-epigenetic interactions, TAD structure, and their biological significance, noting that prior analyses have been limited in scope, typically using 100-500 kb windows that approximate TAD size. TADs are ~1.1 Mb chromatin loops formed by CTCF and cohesin, believed to be largely cell-type invariant and conserved across species, with alterations linked to development and disease.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C17-C23, C75-C76 represent background knowledge and literature review with appropriate citations. These establish the scientific context and motivation for the study. The characterization of prior work limitations (C3, C17) and the correspondence between conventional window sizes and TAD size (C18-C19) provide important context for the study's contributions.

results.result: The authors identified 27,509 significant genetic-epigenetic interaction models from genome-wide regression analysis of 176 DO mouse embryonic stem cell samples. The number of significant models was four orders of magnitude greater than expected under a null distribution, demonstrating that statistical interactions between genetic variants and chromatin accessibility are common throughout the genome.
results.evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding. Reviewer 1 states the manuscript 'reports interactions between genetic variation, DNA accessibility, and chromatin structure in gene expression at a genome wide scale' and calls it 'convincing.' Reviewer 2 describes it as 'important' and notes the authors 'show how the relationships between variants, chromatin, and genes are spatially constrained.' Reviewer 3 states the data are 'of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions.'

results.result: The authors found that genetic-epigenetic interactions occur within the local area of the affected gene and that this locality corresponds to topologically associated domains (TADs). Models with at least one interacting element within the same TAD as the gene were 3.7 times more likely to reach significance, with significant enrichment of intra-TAD gene-peak interactions (odds ratio 1.48, p < 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁶).
results.evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this finding as a key contribution. Reviewer 1 states 'the authors found that most of these interactions occur within topologically associating domains (TADs)' and calls the study 'convincing.' Reviewer 2 emphasizes 'the authors show how the relationships between variants, chromatin, and genes are spatially constrained by topologically associated domains.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the key finding reported here, the importance of 3D chromatin structure in controlling gene expression, although not unexpected, offers a better understanding of the physiological roles of TADs.'

results.result: The authors demonstrate that the likelihood of genetic-epigenetic interaction was most strongly defined by three-dimensional domain structure rather than linear DNA sequence. TAD-based searches produced consistently higher percentages of interacting ATAC-seq peaks compared to linear sequence-based searches, and the gene-centric increase in regulatory interaction density responded to the 3D context of the TAD loop, crossing CTCF boundaries irrespective of linear DNA sequence.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this finding as part of the overall convincing demonstration of TAD importance. Reviewer 1 states '3D genome structure data can be efficiently used to guide the discovery of significant genetic and epigenetic influences on gene expression.' Reviewer 3 notes the study 'offers a better understanding of the physiological roles of TADs' and that the data 'in general support the conclusions made in the manuscript.'

results.result: The authors conclude that stable 3D genome structure is an effective tool to guide searches for regulatory elements, and conversely, that regulatory elements in genetically diverse populations provide a means to infer 3D genome structure. They conclude that genetic and epigenetic factors operate within the context of 3D chromatin structure, and that including TAD boundaries and loops in analyzing genomic features can maximize and contextualize results.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support these conclusions. Reviewer 1 states the study 'highlights the importance of 3D chromatin structure in controlling how gene expression is regulated by genetic and epigenetic processes' and that '3D genome structure data can be efficiently used to guide the discovery of significant genetic and epigenetic influences on gene expression.' Reviewer 3 calls this 'the key finding' and notes it 'offers a better understanding of the physiological roles of TADs.'

results.result: The authors performed CTCF ChIP-seq on mESCs from four DO founder strains and found that 52% of CTCF ChIP-seq peaks were shared across all four strains, with the remaining 48% found in three or fewer strains. They conclude that almost half of CTCF binding is strain specific in mESCs, with imputed links to genetic variants in the DO mouse population, confirming strain-specific binding in the inbred founder mice.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the overall convincing study. Reviewer 3 states 'the experiments described in the manuscript are well designed and executed' and 'most of the data presented are of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions.' No reviewer raises concerns about the ChIP-seq experiments or their interpretation regarding strain-specific CTCF binding.

results.result: The authors found that an increase in ATAC-seq signal had a negative effect on gene expression in 40.76% of models. The negative effector subset was enriched for CTCF-binding sites and SMAD3-binding sites, with 96.1% of CTCF motifs in the negative subset containing SNPs from non-reference DO founder strains versus 18.0% for positive effect-associated CTCF motifs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question this finding. Reviewer 3 states 'most of the data presented are of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions made in the manuscript.' The finding about negative ATAC-seq effects and their association with CTCF binding is presented as part of the overall data supporting the role of 3D chromatin structure, which reviewers explicitly affirm.

results.result: The authors found that the proportion of CTCF ChIP-seq peaks with significant correlation to DO genotype SNPs increased from 16% genome-wide to 31% when subsetting to ATAC-seq peaks, 37% for non-additive interacting models, and 39% for negative effector peaks. In regions with greater than average numbers of regression models, the gap between negative and positive effector regions widened to 44% versus 27% correlation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this analysis as part of the overall convincing demonstration linking genetic variation to CTCF binding and TAD structure. Reviewer 3 notes 'the experiments described in the manuscript are well designed and executed' and the data 'in general support the conclusions.' No reviewer raises concerns about these correlation analyses.

results.result: The authors found that open chromatin participating in the most significant regression models demonstrated enrichment for developmental genes and the TAD-forming CTCF-binding complex, providing an opportunity for statistical inference of shifting TAD boundaries operating during early development.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question this finding. Reviewer 3 states the data are 'of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions' and that the study 'should be of great interest to the field of mammalian gene regulation.' The enrichment for developmental genes and CTCF-binding is presented as supporting evidence for the broader conclusions about TAD function, which reviewers explicitly affirm.

results.result: The authors characterized the spatial distribution of interactions, finding that approximately half (49%) of significant interacting models included elements within 4 Mb of the affected gene, with less than 10% of variants and ATAC peaks clustering closer to each other than to the gene. They found 52,511 ATAC-seq peaks sharing a TAD with their interacting gene versus 24,229 in different TADs, and determined that capturing 95% of inter-TAD interactions required a window of approximately 2 Mb upstream and 2.6 Mb downstream of the gene TSS.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these spatial characterizations as part of the overall convincing demonstration of TAD-constrained interactions. Reviewer 2 explicitly notes 'the authors show how the relationships between variants, chromatin, and genes are spatially constrained by topologically associated domains.' Reviewer 3 states the data 'in general support the conclusions made in the manuscript.'

results.result: The authors found that interacting models represented 32.29% of significant intra-TAD models, with 26.35% of genetic variants shared between non-additive interacting models and additive models, while 41.81% of ATAC-seq peaks were exclusive to interacting models.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these quantitative characterizations of model overlap. Reviewer 3 states 'most of the data presented are of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions.' These findings support the broader conclusion about the importance of non-additive interactions, which reviewers affirm.

results.result: The authors characterized the genomic distribution of ATAC-seq peaks, finding that 65.37% fell within gene bodies, 34.41% within exons (half in the first exon), 24.06% overlapped with promoters, and 6.09% fell within enhancers curated for embryonic stem cell lines.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these descriptive characterizations of ATAC-seq peak distribution. Reviewer 3 states the data are 'of high quality, convincing' and that 'the experiments described in the manuscript are well designed and executed.' These are standard descriptive analyses that support the overall study design.

results.result: The authors characterized the relative magnitudes and types of interaction effects, finding that interaction effects were of greater absolute value than ATAC-seq effects 61.24% of the time. Models indicating redundancy or interference were most common (40.53-39.54%), while synergistic effects were found in 17.02% of models.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these quantitative characterizations of interaction types. Reviewer 3 states 'most of the data presented are of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions.' These findings provide mechanistic detail supporting the broader conclusions about genetic-epigenetic interactions, which reviewers affirm.

results.result: The authors analyzed the Platr2 TAD as a case study, finding 1031 models of non-additive genotype-ATAC interaction reaching significance for resident genes (179 for Platr2 expression). Motif enrichment analysis identified sequences containing Smad3-binding motifs at 16 sites and CTCF-binding motifs at 15 sites, potentially suggesting modulation of CTCF-binding strength.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question this case study analysis. Reviewer 3 states the data are 'of high quality, convincing, and in general support the conclusions.' This example provides specific illustration of the broader findings about TAD-constrained interactions and CTCF involvement, which reviewers explicitly affirm.

results.result: The authors used embryonic stem cells derived from Diversity Outbred (DO) mice, a heterogeneous stock from eight founder strains that segregates millions of variants with linkage disequilibrium blocks approaching TAD size. They profiled 176 samples for genotype, gene expression, and open chromatin.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the experimental system and study design. Reviewer 2 states 'this data set has the ability to add substantial insight into the field' and notes the importance of linking 'gene expression to genetic variants and regions of open chromatin.' Reviewer 3 states 'the experiments described in the manuscript are well designed and executed.' No concerns are raised about the DO mouse system or sample size.

results.result: The authors conclude that integrating analysis of multi-omics data in a genetically diverse population allows for greater specificity and modeling of complex regulatory interactions.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this methodological conclusion. Reviewer 2 states 'this data set has the ability to add substantial insight into the field' and that 'the mechanisms of genetic gene regulation are essential to understanding how standing genetic variation translates to function and phenotype.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the approaches used here can have broader applications in studying genetic and epigenetic regulations of gene expression.'

comparisons.comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C7, C28, C29 regarding widespread genetic-epigenetic interactions. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported with appropriate statistical methods and multiple testing correction.

Both address TAD enrichment (C8, C9, C32) and find strong support. OpenEval emphasizes the 3.7-fold enrichment and statistical evidence, while peer reviewers highlight this as a key contribution showing spatial constraints by TADs.

Both evaluate TAD-based search superiority (C10, C44, C45) and find it well-supported. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation, peer reviewers affirm this demonstrates efficient use of 3D genome structure data for discovery.

Strong agreement on major conceptual conclusions (C11, C12, C16, C71, C77) about TAD importance in gene regulation. Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by the collective evidence, representing key findings of the study.

Both address ChIP-seq validation (C58-C62) and strain-specific CTCF binding (C13, C74 overlap). OpenEval notes sample loss concerns but finds evidence supportive; peer reviewers accept the experiments as well-designed and convincing.

Both evaluate CTCF motif enrichment and negative ATAC effects (C50-C54). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation and notes dramatic SNP content differences; peer reviewers accept findings as high quality and supporting overall conclusions.

Both address progressive enrichment analysis (C65-C69) validating regression models. OpenEval finds strong support with hierarchical validation; peer reviewers accept as part of convincing demonstration linking genetic variation to CTCF binding.

Both evaluate developmental gene enrichment (C14, C15). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculation about shifting TAD boundaries without time-course data; peer reviewers find it SUPPORTED as part of overall convincing findings about TAD function.

Perfect alignment on model overlap quantification (C33-C35). Both find evidence well-supported; OpenEval emphasizes high proportion of interaction-exclusive ATAC peaks, peer reviewers accept as supporting non-additive interaction conclusions.

Both address genomic feature distribution (C40-C43, with C39 in OpenEval). OpenEval notes low enhancer overlap may reflect annotation limitations; peer reviewers accept as high quality descriptive analyses supporting study design.

Both evaluate interaction effect characterization (C47-C49, with C50 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds quantification clear and notes surprising negative ATAC effects; peer reviewers accept as convincing mechanistic detail.

Perfect alignment on Pou5f1 case study (C55-C57). OpenEval finds it well-supported but notes speculative interpretation about CTCF-binding strength modulation; peer reviewers accept as convincing illustration of broader findings.

Both address experimental system and methods (C4-C6, C24-C27). OpenEval finds methods clearly documented with appropriate citations; peer reviewers explicitly affirm study design as well-executed with no concerns about DO system or sample size.

Perfect alignment on methodological conclusion (C70) about multi-omics integration revealing regulatory elements. Both find this general conclusion well-supported by the study's demonstration of interaction-exclusive ATAC peaks and broader applications.

Partial overlap on spatial characterization (C30, C31, C36, C39). OpenEval emphasizes enrichment statistics and co-localization analysis; peer reviewers accept spatial constraints as part of overall TAD-constrained interaction demonstration.
OpenEval evaluates C46 (ATAC peaks close upstream of genes) as SUPPORTED with clear quantitative evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific descriptive finding.

OpenEval evaluates methodological choices (C85-C88) including Bonferroni correction and TAD data sources as SUPPORTED but notes TAD data from single B6 line may not capture strain variation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background/literature review claims (C1-C3, C17-C23, C75-C76) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations establishing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
